name: Ansonica Costa dell'Argentario
terms: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, Italy's top tier. Stricter than DOC, and given only to wines that have been DOC for at least seven years.
Denominazione di Origine Controllata. The label names a precise area, and the wine is tested during production.
Indicazione Geografica Tipica, Italy's broad regional tier.
An aged Italian wine. Chianti Riserva needs at least 6 months in barrel and 3 more in bottle before release.

notes: Sangiovese dominates Tuscany, making powerful, slow-maturing reds.
Brunello di Montalcino is deep, rich and full bodied with well-balanced tannin.
Chianti Classico is medium bodied with firm, dry tannin, smelling of cherry with nutty and floral notes.
Vernaccia di San Gimignano is a dry, full bodied white with earthy notes of honey and minerals.
Tuscan Cabernet Sauvignon has ripe black cherry and strong blackcurrant notes.

blurb.text: A dry white wine from Ansonica, also called Inzolia, on the far southern coast of Tuscany and the island of Giglio. The zone is very sunny, with little rain and dry summers.
